hand.definition: A card player in a game of bridge.

palm.definition: The inner surface of the hand from the wrist to the base of the fingers.

back-of-hand.definition: The outer side of the hand, opposite the palm.
back-of-hand.exampleUsage: A small mark was visible on the back of his hand.

wrist.definition: A joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones.

knuckle.definition: A joint of a finger when the fist is closed.

finger.definition: Any of the terminal members of the hand (sometimes excepting the thumb).

thumb.definition: The part of a glove that provides a covering for the thumb.

index-finger.definition: The finger beside the thumb, often used to point toward things or identify them during classroom activities.

middle-finger.definition: The central finger of the hand, positioned between the index finger and the ring finger.

ring-finger.definition: It is the fourth digit on either hand, positioned between the middle and little fingers.

little-finger.definition: This is the hand’s shortest digit, commonly called the pinky, on the side near the ulna, or forearm bone. It contributes to the precise grip used to hold small objects.

fingerprint.definition: A print made by an impression of the ridges in the skin of a finger.

nail.definition: A small sharp metal pin used to join pieces of wood.

cuticle.definition: The dead skin at the base of a fingernail or toenail.

phalanx.definition: Any of the bones of the fingers or toes.

webbing.definition: Something forming a web (as between the toes of birds).
webbing.exampleUsage: The webbing was identified during the lesson.

crease.definition: An angular or rounded shape made by folding.

squeeze.definition: The act of gripping and pressing firmly.

point.definition: A geometric element that has position but no extension.

snap.definition: The noise produced by the rapid movement of a finger from the tip to the base of the thumb on the same hand.

wave.definition: A movement like that of a sudden occurrence or increase in a specified phenomenon.

clap.definition: To clap one's hands or shout after performances to indicate approval.

fist.definition: A hand with the fingers clenched in the palm (as for hitting).

foot.definition: The part of the leg of a human being below the ankle joint.

heel.definition: The back part of the human foot.

ankle.definition: A gliding joint between the distal ends of the tibia and fibula and the proximal end of the talus.

ball.definition: A round object thrown, kicked, or used in games.

bridge.definition: A structure built over water or a low place for people to cross.

toenail.definition: The nail at the end of a toe.

pedicure.definition: Professional care for the feet and toenails.

nail-polish.definition: A fast-drying cosmetic lacquer applied to the nails to give them color or a glossy finish.

nail-file.definition: A small rough tool used to smooth or shape the edges of fingernails or toenails.
nail-file.exampleUsage: She used a nail file to smooth a rough nail edge.

lotion.definition: A smooth liquid put on the skin to protect or soften it.

moisturizer.definition: A cosmetic product applied to the skin to restore moisture and help prevent dryness.

exfoliant.definition: A product or substance used to remove dead cells from the surface of the skin.
exfoliant.exampleUsage: The foot-care product contains a mild exfoliant.

pumice-stone.definition: A lightweight volcanic rock with many small cavities forms when lava containing trapped gas cools and hardens quickly. Its rough surface makes it useful for scrubbing, while crushed pumice stone can be added to lightweight concrete.

cuticle-oil.definition: A cosmetic oil applied around the base of the nails to moisturize the cuticle area.
cuticle-oil.exampleUsage: She applied cuticle oil around each nail.

hand-cream.definition: A cream applied to the hands to restore moisture and relieve dryness.
